title: FDA Precedents for Drugs in Ultra-Rare and Small-Population Pediatric Cancers
summary: How FDA has handled trial design, endpoints, and confirmatory evidence for drugs in ultra-rare and small-population pediatric cancers.
body_markdown:
## FDA precedents for ultra-rare and small-population pediatric cancer drugs: trial design, endpoints, and evidence of benefit


Pediatric cancers are individually rare, and the ultra-rare subsets (high-risk neuroblastoma, BRAF-altered pediatric low-grade glioma, NTRK-fusion infantile fibrosarcoma, relapsed sarcomas) push against the classical requirement for two adequate and well-controlled randomized trials. FDA's approval record shows a graded approach: a randomized, cooperative-group trial with a survival endpoint when one is feasible, and single-arm designs read out on objective response when it is not. The through-line is that the endpoint and the control strategy are matched to what the disease and the population can realistically support, with confirmatory obligations attached where the evidence is preliminary. The precedents below, drawn from Drugs@FDA approval summaries and review memoranda, map that spectrum.


### The randomized benchmark when a trial is feasible: dinutuximab in high-risk neuroblastoma


Unituxin (dinutuximab) remains the reference point for what FDA expects when a randomized trial can actually be run in a pediatric cancer. Approval in March 2015 rested primarily on Study ANBL0032, a multicenter, open-label, 1:1 randomized trial in newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma patients who had completed induction chemotherapy, autologous stem cell transplant, and radiation and achieved at least a partial response before transplant[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=222)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=223)[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=229)[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=233)[240](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=240) . Critically, this was a cooperative-group study sponsored by the National Cancer Institute's CTEP and conducted by the Children's Oncology Group across 90 sites in the U.S., Canada, and Australia[240](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=240)[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=233)[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=222) , the infrastructure that makes randomization possible in a disease no single sponsor could enroll alone.


The design used a clinical primary endpoint: investigator-assessed event-free survival (EFS), defined as time to relapse, progression, secondary malignancy, or death, with overall survival (OS) as the key secondary endpoint[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=222)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=223)[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=227)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=230)[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=232) . Randomization of 226 patients was stopped early by the Data Safety Monitoring Committee at a planned interim analysis because of the EFS result[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=221)[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=229)[240](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=240) . EFS events were 29% versus 44% (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.37 to 0.89, p = 0.0115 against an allocated alpha near 0.0108), with a supportive OS signal (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.37 to 0.91)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=223)[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=224)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=230)[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=232)[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=234)[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=235)[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=236)[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=238) . FDA noted OS was not formally powered or pre-specified for a definitive comparison, so the approval was driven by EFS from a randomized cooperative-group trial[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=222)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=220)[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=234)[237](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=237) . Unituxin also carried orphan drug designation (granted December 2010), priority review, and rare pediatric disease status[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=209)[210](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=210)[211](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=211)[212](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=212)[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=213)[215](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=215)[217](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=217)[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=219) .


### Single-arm accelerated approval on response endpoints when randomization is not feasible


Where the population is too small or too refractory to randomize, FDA has repeatedly accepted single-arm trials read out on objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) under the accelerated approval pathway.


**Naxitamab (Danyelza)** is the clearest statement of that logic. FDA based the November 2020 accelerated approval on two single-arm, open-label trials in relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma of the bone or bone marrow, with ORR as the major efficacy measure and DOR as the supportive measure[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=246)[247](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=247) . FDA explicitly concluded a randomized trial "would not be feasible" in this rare setting[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=14)[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=22) , recognized a life-threatening disease with no approved therapy[2](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=2)[11](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=11)[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=18) , and narrowed the indication to bone or bone marrow disease with at least stable disease on prior therapy while excluding progressive disease[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=9)[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=19) . As is standard for accelerated approval, FDA attached a confirmatory postmarketing requirement (a multicenter trial of at least 80 patients across a minimum of six sites) to verify benefit[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=6)[24](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=24)[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=25) . Naxitamab carried orphan drug designation (2013) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (2018)[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=288)[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=290) .


**Tovorafenib (Ojemda)** , approved April 2024 for relapsed or progressive pediatric low-grade glioma with an activating BRAF alteration, illustrates a related theme: the endpoint machinery must fit the tumor. The FIREFLY-1 single-arm trial used ORR as the primary endpoint, but FDA judged that the T2/FLAIR-based RAPNO-LGG response criteria were more appropriate for radiographically diffuse pediatric LGG than the HGG criteria and made that secondary endpoint the basis of its efficacy review[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=133)[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=128) . Confirmed ORR by RAPNO-LGG was 53% (39/76) with a median DOR of 18 months[123](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=123)[127](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=127)[132](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=132) , and time-to-event endpoints were treated as descriptive in the single-arm setting[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=128)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=133) . Tovorafenib accumulated Breakthrough Therapy (2020), Orphan Drug (malignant glioma, 2020), and Rare Pediatric Disease designations (2021), plus priority review[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=176)[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=178)[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=179)[180](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=180) .


### Randomizing against active standard of care when an alternative exists


Small population size does not automatically excuse randomization. For BRAF V600E-mutant pediatric low-grade glioma requiring first systemic therapy, dabrafenib plus trametinib (Tafinlar/Mekinist, March 2023) was approved on Study G2201, a multicenter open-label trial that randomized patients 2:1 against carboplatin plus vincristine, the accepted chemotherapy standard[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=107)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=108) . The primary endpoint was independent-review ORR by RANO LGG criteria: 46.6% with the targeted combination versus 10.8% with chemotherapy (p<0.001), with supportive progression-free survival (median 20.1 versus 7.4 months; HR 0.31)[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=107)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=108) . This is the counterpoint to the single-arm cases: where an active comparator exists and enrollment supports it, FDA has held pediatric programs to a randomized, controlled standard even with a response-based primary endpoint.


### Tissue-agnostic pooled analyses and extrapolation into young children


The NTRK-fusion approvals show FDA accepting pooled efficacy across histologies and extrapolating into pediatric ages when the biology is shared.


**Larotrectinib (Vitrakvi)** received accelerated approval in 2018 based on a pooled analysis of the first 55 RECIST-evaluable patients with NTRK-fusion solid tumors across three trials, with a pre-specified success criterion that the lower bound of the 95% CI for ORR exceed 30%[171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=171) . Pooled ORR was 75% (95% CI 61 to 85), and pediatric patients were built into the package: the infantile fibrosarcoma subgroup showed 6 responses in 7 patients (86%), and a pediatric sub-population (N=12) had 100% ORR[166](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=166)[171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=171) . The accelerated approval carried the standard 21 CFR 314.510 obligation to verify benefit with mature response-duration follow-up[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=167)[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=168)[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=169)[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=170) .


**Entrectinib (Rozlytrek)** followed the same pooled tissue-agnostic model on 54 adult NTRK-fusion patients (ORR 57%), with FDA reasoning that ORR can serve as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict benefit when the effect is large and durable[267](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=267)[271](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=271)[270](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=270)[273](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=273) . FDA later extended the indication into children older than one month based on 33 pediatric patients from STARTRK-NG and TAPISTRY (ORR 70%, median DOR 25.4 months), acknowledging limited safety data and requiring a pediatric confirmatory study[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=269)[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=275)[277](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=277) . Both approvals illustrate the acceptance of extrapolation from adult and adolescent data into younger children where the molecular driver is identical.


### The rare-disease and small-population design toolkit in FDA guidance


FDA guidance frames the flexibility these approvals rely on. For pediatric cancer specifically, FDA encourages innovative designs when the population is small, including Bayesian adaptive designs, external controls built from patient-level data, real-world evidence, and alternative outcome measures such as PROs, alongside embedding pediatric cohorts in adult trials, tissue-agnostic development, and master protocols[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=186)[190](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=190)[200](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=200)[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=203) . The RACE for Children Act (FDARA section 505B) requires molecularly targeted pediatric cancer investigations for original NDAs/BLAs of adult cancer drugs whose target is substantially relevant to a pediatric cancer, even where the adult indication never occurs in children and even with orphan designation[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=185)[194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=194)[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=199)[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=202)[207](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=207) . FDA also states that efficacy in adolescents may in some cases be extrapolated from adult data, with independent safety evaluation still required[190](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=190) .


The broader rare-disease guidance sets the evidentiary guardrails: a well-characterized natural history can support planning and, at times, serve as a comparison basis[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=144)[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=146)[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=160) ; external or historical controls are acceptable but are most interpretable when natural history is well defined, groups are closely matched, endpoints are objective, and the treatment effect is large enough to overcome bias[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=145)[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=146)[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=149)[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=152)[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=159)[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=160) ; and single-arm designs with ORR are cited as an appropriate oncology example where meaningful improvement would not occur without intervention[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=146)[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=149)[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=152)[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=158)[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=160) . FDA still expresses a general preference for randomized, controlled trials when feasible and for clinical primary endpoints reflecting how a patient feels, functions, or survives[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=146)[150](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=150)[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=158) .


### Designations and incentives that shape the pathway


The pediatric cancer approvals cluster the same regulatory incentives. Orphan drug designation is near-universal across these products[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=209)[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=288)[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=176)[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=179) . Breakthrough Therapy Designation supported naxitamab and tovorafenib[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=288)[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=290)[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=176)[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=178) . Rare Pediatric Disease designation, which can generate a priority review voucher, appears for dinutuximab and tovorafenib[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=209)[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=179)[180](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=180) , though the voucher mechanics can bite: FDA denied a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher for tovorafenib's second application because a voucher had already been granted under the sponsor's earlier tovorafenib NDA[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=173) . Priority review is essentially standard for this class[217](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=217)[287](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=287)[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=173) .


### What the precedents establish


Read together, the record shows FDA calibrating rather than lowering its evidentiary bar. When a cooperative-group randomized trial with a survival endpoint is achievable, FDA expects it (dinutuximab)[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=222)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=223) . When an active comparator exists and enrollment allows, randomization is still required even with a response endpoint (dabrafenib/trametinib)[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=107)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=108) . When the population is too small or too refractory, FDA accepts single-arm trials read out on ORR and DOR under accelerated approval, with confirmatory studies attached and the indication tightly scoped (naxitamab, tovorafenib)[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=246)[247](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=247)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=133) . Where a molecular driver is shared across histologies and ages, FDA pools efficacy and extrapolates into young children (larotrectinib, entrectinib)[171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=171)[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=269)[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=275) . The recurring features a regulatory team should anticipate are disease-appropriate response criteria (RAPNO-LGG over HGG for pediatric glioma)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=133) , tightly bounded indications tied to the studied population[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=9)[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=19) , confirmatory postmarketing requirements as the price of preliminary evidence[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=6)[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=167) , and early engagement driven by the RACE for Children Act and FDA's rare-disease and pediatric-oncology guidance[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=185)[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-precedents-for-ultra-rare-and-small-population?showSourceNumber=186) .
